nasa-tm-19700025292-an-envelope-of-satur:
H. G. Schaeffer, V. A. Dulock, and J. S. White of the TRW Systems Group wrote this internal note on December 16, 1968. It was prepared for the Manned Spacecraft Center in Houston. It maps the range of Saturn 5 failure paths that could still reach orbit instead of forcing an abort.

Simulation runs test one failure at a time and trace where each path leads. The failures include a platform accelerometer fault, gyro drift, and loss of the inertial attitude reference. Stuck pitch actuators in both stages and an engine out in each stage are covered as well. The note then draws contingency abort limit lines and closes with conclusions and recommendations.
nasa-tm-19710002523-as-508-s-4b-postflig:
W. D. McFadden and I. M. Salzberg wrote this analysis on November 9, 1970. Salzberg, who did the tracking work, was with the Goddard Space Flight Center. The report traces the AS-508 S-IVB stage on its way to a planned crash on the Moon.

The spent stage was aimed at the Moon on purpose. Its impact would shake the lunar ground for a listening instrument. That seismometer had been left by the Apollo 12 crew. The crash served as a known signal to test what the instrument could reveal about the Moon's insides. The report gives the postflight path that the stage actually flew.
